test_title: SSC CGL Tier-II (AAO) 2023 Official Paper-III (Held On: 27 Oct, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which concept enables the accountant to carry forward the values of assets and liabilities from one accounting period to the other without asking the question about usefulness and worth of the assets and recoverability of the receivables?
solution:
The correct answer is** Going Concern Concept.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Going Concern Concept:**

 
 
• This concept assumes that a business will continue to operate indefinitely, and it will not be liquidated in the foreseeable future.
 
• Because of this assumption, accountants can carry forward the values of assets and liabilities from one accounting period to the next without questioning their current usefulness or worth.
 
• This enables the financial statements to be prepared on a historical cost basis rather than a liquidation basis, ensuring consistency and comparability over time.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Business Entity Concept:**

 
 
• This concept states that a business is a separate legal entity from its owners. All financial transactions of the business are recorded separately from the personal transactions of the owners.
 
• While important, this concept does not address the continuation of asset and liability values across accounting periods.
 
 
 
• **Money Measurement Concept:**
 
 
• This concept states that only transactions that can be measured in monetary terms are recorded in the accounting books.
 
• It does not address the continuation of asset and liability values from one period to another.
 
 
 
• **Accounting Period Concept:**
 
 
• This concept states that the life of a business is divided into specific periods (such as months, quarters, or years) for the purpose of financial reporting.
 
• While it helps in preparing periodic financial statements, it does not address the ongoing valuation of assets and liabilities.
